summary: A tree-form spurge native to the Arabian Peninsula, specifically the arid regions of Saudi Arabia and Yemen. Its cactus-like trunk and upward-curving branches form a candelabrum-shaped crown, and leaves appear at branch tips under suitably warm, humid conditions.

A low, spreading evergreen plant endemic to Madagascar, it naturally grows in dry forests, dry shrubland and rocky areas. It blooms from April to June, with flowers ranging from chartreuse and yellow-green to yellow or red, and is threatened by habitat loss.
A plant endemic to Madagascar. It occurs naturally in dry forests and dry shrubland and is threatened by habitat loss.

Perennial flowering plant native to the Iberian Peninsula and North Africa in the western Mediterranean. It has a thick woody base, erect branching stems, yellow nectar glands and black seeds. It grows in forests and damp shrubland, especially beside temporary waterways and in troughs.
A plant native to Madagascar and Europa Island in the Mozambique Channel, it inhabits dry forests, dry shrubland and rocky areas. It is threatened by habitat loss.

An evergreen shrub endemic to the Azores, the Azores tree spurge has robust green stems and thick, leathery, dark blue-green leaves marked with white veins. Its large yellow-green flower heads are strongly honey-scented from May to June.
edibilityNote: The plant is toxic if eaten; its milky white sap may also irritate skin or eyes.

summary: A flowering plant endemic to mainland Portugal. It is protected under Portuguese or European Community legislation, including Annexes II and IV of the Habitats Directive.

A substantial evergreen shrub endemic to Taiwan, where habitat loss threatens it. It has large, hand-shaped leaves and produces spherical clusters of cream or white winter flowers followed by black fruit in spring.

A cactus endemic to the Chihuahuan Desert of northeastern Mexico, where it grows on rocky limestone slopes. It may grow alone or in large clumps, bearing conspicuous red or yellow spines and rings of yellow-to-red flowers around its tip.
Tall semi-deciduous shrub or small tree endemic to the Azores. Fossils suggest it was also native to Madeira before becoming extinct there, and it is threatened by habitat loss.

A thorny shrub native to mainland Portugal. It bears small oblong leaves and yellow flowers in short, loose clusters. In Portugal it grows mainly in wet or peaty heath and scrub in rainy mountain areas.

sources.title: Genista anglica L.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A shrub native to mainland Portugal. It grows around bogs and wet heaths on sandy or peaty ground, chiefly near the coast. It is rare in Portugal, with isolated, scattered populations, and is assessed there as Near Threatened.
A wetland flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. It grows among waterside vegetation beside streams, marshes and ditches, generally on soils derived from siliceous rock.
Flowering plant native to western Mexico and Guatemala.

A small, slow-growing tree native from Mexico through Central America and Florida to the Caribbean and northern South America. Its exceptionally hard, heavy, self-lubricating wood can sink in water, while its dark green leaflets fold together during the hottest part of the day.
A flowering plant native only to Jamaica.

An annual flowering plant endemic to the southwestern coast of mainland Portugal. It grows in open patches on sandy-clay ground, including coastal scrub clearings, cliffs, rocks and dunes; it was assessed as Endangered in mainland Portugal, with ongoing habitat decline and uncertainty over its two northernmost populations.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Herniaria algarvica
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

summary: A flowering plant endemic to coastal Portugal, Herniaria maritima inhabits clearings among creeping woodland and junipers on fixed coastal dunes. It grows on sandy soils that are neutral or alkaline.
A flowering perennial native to Western Europe. It forms greyish mats with creeping, rooting stems, rounded hairy leaves, and resin-scented yellow flowers whose petals are edged with red dots.
A small terrestrial herb of high Andean forests and páramo in Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Venezuela and Bolivia. Its flowers are usually yellow or white, but are rarely purple or orange.

An evergreen shrub or small tree native to Madeira and the Canary Islands. It has glossy leaves with mostly rounded edges and few spines, though young leaves can be thorny, followed by small white flowers and red fruits.
Perennial plant found from eastern France to Sweden and in the mountains of Uzbekistan. Its leaves are woolly on both sides, and its small flower heads contain bright golden-yellow florets.

A tree fern native to parts of China and the western Malay Peninsula. It is often prostrate, forming colonies on open forest slopes and disturbed ground, and has a woolly rhizome. Extensive collection in Southeast Asia has reduced its populations.
An annual flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. It grows in dry, sandy annual grassland within openings in scrub and woodland.

A perennial aquatic herb native from Europe to Siberia and the western Himalaya, it grows in quiet freshwater such as ponds, lakes and slow streams. Its floating flowers have numerous white petals surrounding a red or yellow centre.

A perennial aquatic plant endemic to western Europe and associated with fast-flowing water. It lacks floating leaves, instead bearing long, narrow, tassel-like segments. White flowers rise above the water and have overlapping petals around a yellow centre.

Soft-wooded herbaceous plant native to much of Africa, including Madagascar, and southwestern and southern Asia. It is deep-rooted and often erect, with broad leaves and thick white flower clusters whose fibres were traditionally harvested in Arabia for stuffing cushions and saddle pads.

An aquatic flowering plant native to the Azores, Morocco, Iceland, the Faroes and most of Europe except the dry southeast. It usually grows submerged in nutrient-poor freshwater and takes in most of its carbon dioxide through its roots; if falling water exposes them, it stops using one of its two photosynthetic processes.

summary: A small creeping herb found in shallow water around European lakes and pools. Its stems root where leaves emerge, and its yellow-green submerged foliage can turn bright green or reddish on exposed mud.

A flowering plant commonly found in New Zealand from sea level to about 900 metres. It has long, sword-like green leaves, sometimes with red midribs, followed by central green flowers in October and November and yellow-orange summer fruit.

A medium-sized tree fern native to New Zealand. It is slow-growing and long-lived, with a thick, soft, rusty-brown fibrous trunk and a distinctive skirt of retained dead leaves. A local Tauranga variety regularly branches into numerous forks.

A shrub or small tree with subspecies native to New Zealand and Norfolk Island, māhoe bears flowers and purple fruits directly on woody stems. Its fallen leaves often decay between the veins, leaving distinctive skeleton-like remains.

A deciduous shrub native to central and southern Europe, North Africa and the Middle East. It has white spring flowers and small black ripe fruits, which are edible raw or cooked but are bland and often made into jam, compote or spirits.
edibilityNote: The fruits are edible raw or cooked; they are bland and often processed into jam, compote or spirits.

summary: A climbing wild rose native to the mountains of central and southern Europe, it bears fragrant deep-pink flowers and relatively few thorns. Its oblong hips hang downwards.
A rhizomatous aquatic perennial native to subarctic and temperate Eurasia. Its submerged leaves are round and wrinkled, and its faintly fragrant yellow flowers have a star-shaped central disk.
A flowering plant native from Europe to the Russian Far East, commonly called eight-stamened waterwort.

An aquatic subshrub native across scattered parts of the Mediterranean, western and eastern Europe, the eastern Mediterranean and western Himalayas. It has simple, broad leaves and remains low-growing.

An aquatic or marsh flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. In Portugal it is associated with slightly saline water. Its brown fruit has four blunt, rounded edges, a feature reflected in its common name.

sources.title: Callitriche obtusangula Le Gall
sources.attribution: Info Flora, plazi (2021). Info Flora Schweiz - Plantaginaceae. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/u7jmcd accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A compact evergreen fern endemic to New Zealand, where it grows in scrub and forests. Its fronds can carry more than 30 pairs of round, dark-green, leathery leaflets.
Wild barley native to Europe, including Madeira, Crimea and the northern Caucasus, as well as northwestern Africa and the Levant. It has been introduced to Australia and New Zealand.

A large cactus native to Baja California, Baja California Sur and Sonora in northwestern Mexico. It is exceptionally tall, heavily branched and bears large white flowers that open at night. Its fruits were traditionally an important food for the Seri people of Sonora.
edibilityNote: The fruits were traditionally an important food for the Seri people of Sonora.

summary: A columnar cactus endemic to Mexico, Indian comb forms a tall, many-branched tree. Its white flowers open in the evening and close by midday, while its golden-spined fruits split when ripe to reveal red, juicy pulp and black seeds.
edibilityNote: Fruit is eaten raw or cooked and made into syrup, preserves, jam or wine; the Mayo historically made foods from ground seeds and cornmeal.

summary: A marine red alga of unspecified native origin, it occurs in Guam and the Houtman Abrolhos and was introduced to Hawaii from Guam in 1950. It reproduces sexually and through fragmentation, and even small amounts of remaining tissue can regrow rapidly.

A perennial flowering plant native to KwaZulu-Natal and the Eastern Cape in South Africa, it is widely grown in gardens. Its open-faced blue, purple or white flowers appear from late spring to summer, and its powerful roots can break concrete.
edibilityNote: The leaves of subspecies orientalis are poisonous.

summary: A large shrub or small tree native to Japan, Taiwan, southern and eastern China, and Vietnam, Taiwan cherry blooms early and has characteristic bell-shaped flowers. It is widely grown as an ornamental but is invasive in some parts of New Zealand.

Subtropical palm native to southern Japan, Taiwan, the Ryukyu Islands, southeastern China and Hainan. It has fan-shaped leaves and can become invasive in some wetlands and island ecosystems outside its native range.

A flowering tree native to eastern Australia, it may begin life growing on another plant or on rocks. Mature trees have spreading crowns and yellow-brown buttressed trunks; rusty leaf undersides help distinguish them from similar figs. Their small yellow figs ripen red throughout the year, especially in spring and summer.

An aquatic or semiterrestrial succulent originally from Australia and New Zealand. Its stiff shoots carry narrow opposite leaves, and it forms dense carpets along muddy pond margins or elongated growth underwater without dying back in winter.

A perennial grass native to most of Africa, southern Asia, southern Iran and Sicily, buffelgrass is deep-rooted and drought-tolerant. Where invasive, it spreads quickly, ignites readily and regrows rapidly after fire.

A flowering prickly poppy native to Mexico, Mexican poppy has sticky yellow sap. Introduced widely beyond Mexico, it has become invasive in Australia, Africa, tropical Asia, New Zealand and several oceanic islands.

A creeping plant native to dry parts of the Mediterranean Basin in North Africa, southern Europe and West Asia. It grows on rocky coastlines, with fleshy leaves, narrow-petalled violet flowers and many small fruits near its thorns.

summary: A perennial herb native to the Canary Islands, southern Portugal and parts of the Mediterranean. It bears vivid yellow, daisy-like flowers with darker centres and thrives in dry coastal settings, often on sandy soil.

A small deciduous tree native to the Mediterranean region, including the Sahara in Morocco, and to Somalia. It has shiny green leaves and rounded dark-yellow fruit described as edible, although that claim is marked as needing citation.
edibilityNote: The rounded dark-yellow fruit is described as edible, although the source marks this claim as needing citation.

summary: A woody plant native to mainland Portugal and Madeira. In Portugal it grows in hedges and degraded scrub on nitrogen-rich soils near the coast, sometimes along roadside verges and banks.

sources.title: Lycium europaeum L.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: Annual herb native to much of the United States, eastern Canada, Mexico, Central America, the Caribbean and Venezuela. It grows upright with paired oblong, finely toothed leaves that may be hairy or smooth. Its flower structures can be solitary or clustered, with flat white or red appendages surrounding the flowers.

An annual herb native to the Caribbean, Central America, Mexico, most of South America and most of the United States. Its slender, sometimes purple-tinted stems trail along the ground, bearing finely toothed oval leaves and tiny, often hard-to-detect flowers.

Annual herb native to the Americas, matted sandmat grows as a low mat of spreading stems that root where their joints touch the ground. Its tiny paired oval leaves accompany scalloped white, petal-like structures with red nectar glands.

Evergreen perennial native to China, India, Japan, Nepal and Vietnam. It forms ground-covering sod with narrow leaves, white to pale-lilac flowers and blue berries. Large spreading stems and tuberous roots grow underground.
An annual herb native to Australia and New Zealand. It has green or white flowers and favours well-drained sites, especially those with calcareous soils.

A palm native to northern and western Africa, the Levant and Arabian Peninsula. Its trunk forks into branches topped by fan-shaped leaves, while female trees bear woody, single-seeded fruits that remain on the tree for long periods.
edibilityNote: Fruit rind and pulp, unripe kernels, germinated seed shoots, young-fruit juice and sap are consumed in foods, drinks and palm wine.

summary: Fast-growing evergreen tree native to New Zealand. It has a rounded crown of dense foliage and leathery, glossy yellow-green leaves. Small greenish flowers appear from late spring to midsummer, followed by dark purple or black berries that ripen from autumn to winter.

An evergreen tree endemic to New Zealand, tarata has yellow-green, curly-edged leaves that smell strongly of lemon when crushed. Fragrant yellow-cream spring flowers are followed by black seed capsules, and young conical trees become rounded as they mature.

A large deciduous oak tree native to most of Europe and extending into Anatolia and Iran, the sessile oak has stalked, evenly lobed leaves and stalkless acorns. Its male flowers appear in spring, and its acorns mature in about six months.

A green seaweed of unspecified native origin, it occurs widely in coastal waters and intertidal pools. It is bright green with a soft, silky texture and branches arranged in two opposite rows; fertile males become yellowish-green while females remain dark green.
A green alga found in the British Isles and other coastal locations. It forms bright green tubes or flat strips, often with ruffled edges, and is edible.
edibilityNote: The species is edible and can be used as food.

summary: An evergreen shrub native to Mexico and Central America. It has a thick, often elephant-foot-like base and clumps of narrow, spineless leaves. In Central America, flower petals are eaten after the bitter anthers and ovaries are removed, then blanched and cooked; tender stem tips are eaten in El Salvador.
edibilityNote: Flower petals are eaten after bitter reproductive parts are removed, then blanched and cooked; tender stem tips are eaten in El Salvador.

summary: Large palm native to Mexico, the Caribbean, Florida and parts of Central America. It has a stout, exceptionally smooth grey-white trunk with a characteristic bulge beneath its green crown, while its fruit darkens from green through red to purplish-black.

Deciduous tree native to southern Mexico, El Salvador, Guatemala, Hispaniola, Honduras, Nicaragua and Cuba. It has succulent stems and fragrant, sticky, cotton-candy-pink flowers packed with hundreds of stamens. In Central America, a highly intoxicating drink is made from the tree, though the part and preparation are unspecified.
edibilityNote: In Central America, a highly intoxicating drink is made from the tree; the part and preparation are unspecified.

summary: A flowering tree native to Mexico, the American coral tree has bright red flowers shaped like little machetes. In southern Mexico, only the red part of the flower is boiled and cooked with scrambled eggs or tuna; the seeds and rest of the tree are described as highly toxic.
edibilityNote: In southern Mexico, only the red flower parts are boiled and cooked with eggs or tuna; seeds and other parts are highly toxic.

summary: A woody perennial tree found in Mexico, the southeastern USA, and parts of Central America and the Caribbean, it has reddish to red-purple bark that peels away in papery sheets. Its clustered flowers range from white to Mexican pink, while its ripe yellow fruit is edible and used in alcoholic drinks, syrups, jams and soups.
edibilityNote: Ripe fleshy fruits are edible; the sweet-and-sour fruits are used in alcoholic drinks, liqueurs, syrups, jams and soups.

summary: An evergreen tree or shrub native to the tropical rainforests of West and Central Africa, the fiddle-leaf fig has large, leathery leaves shaped like a fiddle. Their prominent veins and wavy edges make the plant especially distinctive.

A deciduous plane tree native to northeastern and central Mexico and Guatemala. Its five-lobed leaves have dark, waxy upper surfaces and much paler undersides covered with fine white hairs, turning yellowish brown in autumn.
A flowering shrub native to eastern Madagascar, although its natural distribution is poorly understood. It has heart-shaped, serrated leaves and hanging clusters of fragrant pink flowers.

A large evergreen tree native to eastern Australian rainforests and nearby southwest Pacific islands, including Vanuatu and New Caledonia. It bears red-and-yellow flowers and cylindrical pods containing large, chestnut-like seeds.
edibilityNote: Raw seeds are poisonous; Aboriginal preparation made them edible by roasting, cutting, prolonged leaching, pounding into flour and roasting again, for at least 2,500 years.

summary: A plant endemic to Mexico and Mesoamerica. Its clear sap can blister or irritate skin, and ingestion can cause vomiting and diarrhea.
edibilityNote: Ingestion can cause vomiting and diarrhea.

summary: A perennial, semi-woody shrub reported from the North Atlantic region, especially dry grassy and rocky places across much of Europe. It has white flowers with yellow centres and evergreen, narrow leaves covered in greyish or whitish hairs, especially underneath.

A rhizomatous herbaceous perennial endemic to south-central Chile, it produces tall flower stalks and elongated leaves. Its lilac-to-whitish flowers have yellow bands and wine-red streaks on the inner segments.

A bulbous flowering perennial native to mainland Europe, excluding the British Isles, and Turkey. It grows in dry pastures, rocky places and open woods, producing narrow leaves and clusters of lily-like white flowers in spring and summer.

summary: An asphodel-family plant native to North Africa, Southern Europe, the Middle East and South Asia, it has a fibrous root system. It has been introduced to Australia and the Mascarene Islands.

A flowering herb native to tropical and temperate Asia and Africa. It has succulent, triangular to egg-shaped leaves, while its inner flower parts enlarge into papery structures around persistent, hard red fruits with a netted pattern.
Small, stemless aloe native to South Africa. Its blue-green leaves have sometimes faint lengthwise lines and smooth pink margins, and it bears red flowers.

An orchid native to the Mediterranean, growing in damp meadows, open fields, marshes and sometimes scrub. Its flower spikes appear from April to May or early June, with lips ranging from yellowish through pink to magenta; southern English records may not be naturally occurring.
A perennial herb native to mainland Portugal. It inhabits peat bogs, marshes and other very wet places, usually near the coast, and has disappeared from several historically recorded sites.

summary: An aquatic fern native to numerous countries across Africa and Asia, as well as Brazil, Trinidad and Tobago, and several Indian Ocean islands. It creeps and spreads in water but may form cushions on land, with adults typically growing terrestrially. It is eaten in India, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh, though the plant part and preparation are not specified.
edibilityNote: Eaten in India, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh; the plant part and preparation are not specified.

summary: A small, delicate fern occurring across the Mediterranean basin, it depends on seasonal flooding in temporary freshwater pools. Its spores survive the dry period but germinate only when the ground is completely saturated.

summary: A wetland flowering plant with no species-wide native origin supplied, although subsp. baetica is native to mainland Portugal. Its subspecies occupy pond margins, temporary pools, peat bogs and springs, sometimes favouring acidic ground.
A flowering plant in the mustard family, recorded from mainland Portugal and the Azores. The supplied account does not give an unambiguous native origin.

A small red marine alga whose native origin is not stated, it grows upright with cylindrical, repeatedly branched filaments. It occurs in rock pools and shallow coastal waters across the British Isles, but is very difficult to distinguish from some related species.

Salt-loving annual succulent found beside saline water in Europe. Its jointed bright-green stems turn red or purple in autumn, and it has tiny scale-like leaves. It is edible raw or cooked and is usually cooked in unsalted water because of its high salt content.
edibilityNote: It is eaten raw or cooked and is usually boiled in plenty of unsalted water because the plant is naturally salty.

summary: A flowering plant native to Mexico, it grows mainly in deserts or dry shrubland. Many small, green succulent leaves cluster densely around its stems.

A spreading evergreen shrub native to China and the Himalayas, bright bead cotoneaster has arching greenish to purple-black branches and leaves with hairy undersides when young. Clusters of berries appear after its white flowers.

A deciduous shrub native to Japan, Korea and northeastern China, border privet has relatively small leaves. It is invasive in parts of the United States and has become particularly common around southern New England, the mid-Atlantic and the Great Lakes.

A perennial herb native to Eurasia, from Europe east to western Siberia, autumn hawkbit has branched stems bearing several bright yellow flower heads. It flowers from June to October and is frequent in damp grassland and meadows.

A perennial sedge of circumboreal mountain regions, tufted bulrush grows in wet, acidic bogs, moorland and heaths. It forms dense tufts of wiry stems, with leaves reduced to pointed basal sheaths and very small brownish flower heads at the tips.

summary: A flowering plant native to Europe and now widespread in the United States. Its pink or lavender flower clusters rise above sticky stem areas that trap small insects, although the plant is not currently regarded as carnivorous.

An annual grass native to Eurasia and naturalized in North America. Its harsh, hairy stems, leaves and flower branches bear reddish spikelets with long awns. Its seeds and awns can penetrate livestock skin, mouths, eyes and intestines.

A low-growing, hairless perennial flowering plant native to Europe and Western Asia, lesser celandine has fleshy, heart-shaped dark green leaves and glossy bright yellow flowers. It emerges in late winter and can form extensive carpets; in North America it is introduced and invasive. Raw plants are poisonous, but cooking or drying removes toxicity, and Mesolithic Europeans ate the roots boiled, fried or roasted.
edibilityNote: Cooked or dried plants have been eaten; Mesolithic Europeans ate roots boiled, fried or roasted. Raw plants are poisonous.

summary: A perennial herb native to eastern Asia. Its summer flowers are orange-red with darker spots, and its autumn seed pods open to reveal shiny black seed clusters resembling blackberries.

A perennial flowering rush from northwestern Africa, almost all of Europe and the Caucasus, and introduced elsewhere. It forms large, dense tufts with vivid green, ribbed stems and a spherical flower head that appears to grow from the stem's side.

Perennial flowering plant native to Europe, western Asia and parts of the Middle East. It is the only member of its genus with yellow flowers and has square stems with paired, toothed leaves that may bear silvery markings.

An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows mainly in sparse meadows, pastures and openings in dry scrub or woodland on sandy, acidic ground; its flower clusters vary considerably in hairiness.

summary: Downy perennial flowering plant native to Eurasia. It has strongly veined, unstalked leaves and tiny greenish-white, funnel-shaped flowers that appear in June and July. The fruits split into four shiny white nutlets that can persist into winter.

A small annual flowering plant native to Europe and parts of North Africa, possibly extending into western Asia, it is usually grey-green and covered with short, fluffy hairs. Its tiny yellow flower heads begin as five-sided pyramids and open into star shapes.
Small perennial herb native widely across North America and Eurasia. It grows in moist soils and seasonal pools.
Plant species native to much of Europe and Asia. Known as sickle alfalfa or yellow lucerne, it forms a nitrogen-fixing partnership with the bacterium Sinorhizobium meliloti.
An aquatic plant widespread across Europe and Asia and naturalized in many other regions. It generally grows in wet places at lower elevations.

Flowering plant native to the central United States, it may grow as an annual, biennial or perennial. Its simple leaves alternate along the stem, while its four-petalled flowers range from white or pink to red.

Biennial flowering plant native to eastern and central North America, reaching north to Quebec. Its upper flowering stems have soft white hairs, and its light pink flowers turn vivid red-pink in late summer to early autumn.

An herb native to Southeast Asia, small water-pepper has creeping, slender stems, narrow tapering leaves and minute pale-violet flowers. In Malaysia and Indonesia, its shoots and young leaves are eaten raw in salads, used to flavour peppery dishes, or made into tea.
edibilityNote: In Malaysia and Indonesia, shoots and young leaves are eaten raw in salads, added to peppery dishes for aroma, or used as tea leaves.

summary: A low-growing succulent native to rocky upland meadows in Georgia, northern Iran and northeastern Turkey. Its creeping stems root as they spread, while its flowers range from white to deep red and its upper leaves turn burgundy in autumn.

A deciduous shrub or small tree native to the listed regions of mainland Portugal. It is highly branched and sometimes thorny, with twisting reddish-brown branches and white flowers. Its fruit may be eaten cooked or raw when fully ripe; the flowers and oil contained in the seeds are also edible.
edibilityNote: Fruit is eaten cooked or raw when fully ripe; flowers are used as garnish or tea, and the seed contains edible oil.

summary: A climbing perennial rose native to the Mediterranean, the evergreen rose has very prickly stems and glossy leaves that persist through much of winter. Its slightly fragrant white flowers bloom from May to July.

An annual herb with a broad Old World distribution from North Africa through Europe into Asia, though its native origin is not explicitly stated. In Portugal it occurs in damp coastal grassland and salt marshes.

A flowering plant native across Europe eastward to West Siberia and Kazakhstan. It usually grows in fens and damp meadows, though continental records include oakwoods and hot, dry limestone. Crushed foliage has a mildly parsley-like scent.
edibilityNote: Food or seasoning records are hard to find, but the plant is not listed as poisonous.

summary: Deciduous shrub native to the Carpathian Mountains of Romania and western Ukraine. It bears strongly fragrant, dark pink flowers in slender clusters in early summer and has a very restricted wild range.

A slow-growing, slender date palm native to southeastern Asia, from southwestern China through northern Laos to northern Vietnam. Its many grey-green leaflets droop slightly, and it bears small yellowish flowers followed by edible, thin-fleshed, date-like fruit.
edibilityNote: The small, thin-fleshed, date-like fruit is edible.

summary: A flowering plant native to central and southern Mexico. Its thick, dark-green, spiny leaves form a spiral rosette and leave imprints on underlying leaves. It flowers once, usually after 15–25 years, producing a tall stalk of greenish-yellow flowers before dying.

A cactus native to Mexico in North America. It forms a tree-like shrub with upright branches and yellow-to-orange flowers; its yellow-green, red-tinged fruit is edible but bears small bristles and spines.
edibilityNote: The yellow-green, red-tinged fruit is edible and is covered with small bristles and spines.

summary: A small succulent perennial found in the Chihuahuan Desert of Coahuila, Durango and Nuevo León, Mexico. Its compact rosettes have rigid green leaves patterned with distinctive white lines, usually without marginal teeth but ending in one to three spines.

A tree-forming flowering plant native to Puebla and northern Oaxaca in Mexico, it is endemic to the Tehuacán Valley scrubland. Older plants develop a greatly swollen trunk base and carry erect, blue-grey leaves with finely rough, sharp margins.

A small evergreen shrub native from Italy north to Austria and Slovakia and east to Turkey and Crimea. It has flattened, leaf-like stems bearing tiny true leaves and yellow flowers; male and female flowers occur on separate plants, and red berries are rarely produced.

Shrubby cactus occurring in the temperate, dry parts of central Mexico. It can form closed stands and has unusually large pads; its yellow flowers mature into reddish, sweet-and-sour fruit used for drinks, preserves, sweets and spirits.
edibilityNote: The fruit is prepared as fresh juice, preserves, sweets, crystallized fruit, dried fruit, wine and spirits.

summary: A fleshy perennial native to the Mediterranean Basin and Middle East, from the Azores to Oman. It has very succulent dark-green leaf rosettes and pale-green, bell-shaped flowers held horizontally rather than drooping.
An orchid occurring from Peru to Bolivia.
Tree native to Mexico, Guatemala, Honduras and El Salvador. It has a swollen trunk base, furrowed bark and slender leaves, and grows in deciduous tropical forests.
An evergreen flowering perennial endemic to eastern Mexico, elephant’s-foot is not a true palm. It has a greatly swollen, water-storing trunk base and terminal tufts of recurved, leathery leaves.

Tree endemic to Oaxaca, Mexico, where it grows in dry forests and shrublands. Its stem expands into a large circular base beneath long, straight, thin leaves. It is considered vulnerable and is threatened by habitat conversion and illegal collection for ornamental trade.
An orchid native from Chiapas in southern Mexico through Central America to Costa Rica. It is Costa Rica's national flower.

A flowering shrub native to the tropical Americas from extreme southern Mexico and Belize through much of Central America and northern South America, including many Caribbean islands. It grows upright on cane-like stems and has large green leaves, often patterned with white. Its sap is toxic, and ingesting any part may cause severe reactions or death.
edibilityNote: The entire plant contains calcium oxalate crystals; ingestion may cause anaphylactic shock, respiratory failure or death.

summary: Flowering vine of unspecified native origin, widespread across much of Central and South America. Its thick, waxy, heart-shaped leaves have large oval holes.

A palm found throughout Mexico and Central America, it grows in colonies from short horizontal stems at or below ground, forming dense or open clumps. Its round fruits turn from green to black or purple-black as they ripen.
An evergreen, trunk-forming shrub native to the Chihuahuan Desert and other dry habitats of northeastern Mexico. It grows slowly and bears exceptionally long, narrow blade-like leaves.
An orchid occurring from Mexico to Colombia and southeastern Brazil. Its seeds are exceptionally small.
A cactus endemic to Mexico’s Central Plateau. It is the largest and tallest Astrophytum species, with a solitary cylindrical body, white woolly flakes and canary-yellow summer flowers.
A cactus native to central Mexico. Its solitary spherical stems are covered in white down and spines, and its reddish-purple spring and summer flowers sometimes form a complete ring around the tip.

A flowering cactus native to northeastern Mexico. Its clustered round stems are hidden beneath white, downy spines with long hairs arranged like bird-feather segments. White or greenish-yellow flowers appear in late summer.
Cactus native to southern Mexico, where it is endemic to moist lowland rainforest. It has unusual flat, leaf-like stems and fragrant flowers that open for only one night.

An evergreen succulent native to semi-desert areas of Mexico and common throughout Puebla, the Mexican firecracker forms rounded rosettes of fleshy, spoon-shaped leaves covered in irritating white hairs. In spring it produces red flowers with yellow tips on tall stalks.

A cactus with no explicitly stated native origin, widely distributed across several central and southern Mexican states and Mexico City. Usually solitary but sometimes producing offsets with age, it has dense white bristly spines, deep pink to crimson flowers and red fruits.

summary: A flowering cactus from Hidalgo, Mexico, the rattail cactus grows on rocks or other plants in dry forests and seems rare and seldom collected in the wild. Its profusely branching stems eventually trail and bear bristle-like spines, while its scentless crimson flowers open by day for three to five days.

Evergreen succulent perennial native to semi-desert habitats in Mexico. It forms compact rosettes of pale blue-green fleshy leaves and bears pink, yellow-tipped flowers in winter and spring. It also produces multiple offsets.

A rosette-forming plant with no explicitly stated native origin, known from a valley in Oaxaca, Mexico. Its thick leaves have a striking powdery grey-blue or occasionally pinkish surface, while its red, frosted-looking flowers appear from October to March.

summary: A deciduous tree native to Mexico and endemic to cloud forests in northern Oaxaca, this magnolia has exceptionally broad leaves and large white flowers. It was once thought extinct but was rediscovered in 1977.

A short-trunked plant from northeastern Mexico, Berlandier’s sotol grows on open rocky ground and in open woodland. Its thin, waxy blue leaves vary in appearance and have irregular upward-pointing edge spines. Numerous green to yellow flowers appear from May to June on a tall, narrow, woody flower stalk.

Cactus native to north-central Mexico, growing on canyon walls and volcanic rock in semi-desert. White hair-like spines conceal radial and hooked central spines; cream flowers are followed by cylindrical red fruit.

A cylindrical cactus endemic to Guerrero and Morelos in central Mexico, it inhabits dry tropical forest and arid scrub at roughly 1,600–1,900 metres. Red-brown or white spines cover the stem, while pink funnel-shaped flowers form a ring around its tip and produce bright red berries.

A solitary cactus of unstated native origin, it is distributed across Coahuila, Durango, Nuevo León and Tamaulipas in Mexico. Its blue-green body bears abundant milky sap and a strong black central spine, while its flowers range from whitish to vivid pink or crimson.

A cluster-forming cactus native to Jalisco and Aguascalientes in western-central Mexico. Dense white wool surrounds its tightly packed tubercles and numerous white spines, with longer curved brown spines standing out. Rings of deep pink flowers appear across the upper surface in spring and summer.

Tree fern native to the tropical and subtropical Americas, from southern Mexico through Central and South America. It has an upright cylindrical trunk and large, twice-divided fronds, and illegal extraction puts it at risk of extinction.

Herbaceous perennial native to temperate Europe, Mediterranean Europe, North Africa, western Asia, the Caucasus, Iraq and Iran. It has square stems with conspicuous winged corners, while its paired leaves bear many translucent dots and its pale yellow flowers grow in clusters.
A flowering plant whose native origin is stated only for subsp. crispa, which is endemic to mainland Portugal.

A flowering plant from Europe and the Mediterranean, early star-of-Bethlehem usually blooms from January to March or April. It has yellow, six-petalled flowers and twisting, thread-like basal leaves, and grows mainly in dry grassland.

Tree endemic to south-eastern continental Australia. Its rough, flaky or fibrous trunk bark contrasts with smoother pale bark above, and it bears white flowers in groups of seven; honey produced from it is renowned for its quality.
edibilityNote: Honey produced from the tree is renowned for its quality.

summary: A large woodland and forest tree native to eastern Australia, it has fibrous grey bark and a broad, often gnarled form. Cream-white flowers appear from November to March, and it typically grows on floodplains and along watercourses in alluvial soils.
A tree endemic to southeastern Australia. It has smooth white-to-yellowish bark, lance-shaped adult leaves and white flowers, with flower buds grouped in threes or sevens depending on subspecies.

A small to medium-sized tree endemic to southeastern Australia. Its smooth, powdery grey or pink bark peels in long ribbons, and it has white flowers in groups of three followed by woody cup-shaped or bell-shaped fruit.
Shrub-like perennial native to Mexico, tree stonecrop is a hardy garden plant whose leaves turn red in winter.

A trailing annual herb, Algerian tea occurs around the Mediterranean in dry or disturbed ground, dunes and ditches. Its tiny flowers are gathered in clusters and surrounded by conspicuous silvery, scale-like bracts.
A plant native to Mexico, Central America and South America. It has very short leaf stalks and small leaves and was traditionally used in Peruvian herbal medicine.
A flowering sedge found across most of Europe, including Britain, as well as Northwest Asia and North America. It can grow into a tall tussock.
A red alga distributed throughout tropical to warm-temperate waters worldwide. In Hawaiian cuisine it is a bitter, iodine-like condiment traditionally added to poke.
edibilityNote: Traditionally used in Hawaiian cuisine as a bitter condiment and poke ingredient.

summary: A flowering shrub native to tropical Asia, specifically Malesia and Papuasia, chenille plant has separate male and female plants. Female plants bear long, hanging clusters of furry purple-to-bright-red flowers, with large leaves ranging from bright green to reddish copper.
A palm tree endemic to Palawan and Danjugan Island in the Philippines. Its fruits become bright scarlet, usually in winter, inspiring the name Christmas palm.
edibilityNote: Its fruits are sometimes said to substitute for betel nut in buyo prepared for chewing.

summary: A dwarf evergreen shrub or small tree of unknown wild origin, found in Japan and Taiwan. It has bright green oval leaves with rounded or notched tips and is widely shaped into hedges, topiary and bonsai.

A grass-like sedge native to West Africa, Madagascar and the Arabian Peninsula, umbrella papyrus is widely grown as an ornamental in gardens, ponds, pots and homes. It needs abundant moisture, can grow in shallow water and requires protection from cold weather.

A tall, branching annual herb of uncertain origin, with one subspecies originating in India and another in America. Young leaves are hairy and magenta before turning green. Its young shoots and leaves are eaten cooked, or raw in small quantities, while the seeds are prepared like rice or quinoa or ground for flour.
edibilityNote: Young shoots and leaves are cooked or eaten raw sparingly; seeds are cooked like grain or ground into flour.

summary: A perennial clover native to Europe. Its flowers are yellowish-white, and it grows in grassy places, especially on clay soils.

An erect or reclining herb widespread across Europe, Asia, Africa and Canada, false cleavers is considered a noxious weed in many places. It has square stems, narrow leaves arranged in whorls and white or yellow-green flowers.
A palm native and endemic to Round Island, Mauritius. Its trunk swells near the base and tapers upward, and it carries only four to six open leaves at a time.
Aquatic plant native to Southern Africa. It is used in freshwater aquariums but is invasive in some countries and legally restricted in the European Union.

An evergreen tree native to China, banana shrub bears strongly fragrant cream-white flowers, sometimes with yellow or purple colouring. Its flower buds and new leaves have a velvet-like covering, while mature leaves are leathery and glossy dark green.
A plant native from the Solomon Islands to Vanuatu. It is widely grown as an ornamental beyond its native range and has been introduced to many tropical countries.
Azalea species native to southern and western Honshu, Shikoku, Kyushu and Yakushima in Japan. Its many cultivars include the Satsuki azaleas.

An evergreen tree native to South and Southeast Asia, although its exact origin is unknown. It has yellow flowers and compound leaves with paired leaflets, and is often planted for shade in cocoa, coffee and tea plantations.
edibilityNote: Leaves, tender pods and seeds are eaten in Burmese and Thai cooking only after boiling and discarding the water; buds also feature in Burmese dishes.

summary: An aquatic flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. A 2020 mainland assessment found it very scattered, absent from many historical sites but present in some newly discovered populations, and classified it as Vulnerable.

summary: A perennial vine native to Europe, with paired, pointed leaves and small star-shaped flowers ranging from dark purple to black. Its slender seed pods contain seeds with fluffy tufts that carry them on the wind.

A perennial plant occurring from northeastern Spain through central Mediterranean countries to northern Europe, Asia Minor and Tunisia. It has glossy leaflets, pale yellow flowers and segmented cylindrical seed pods, and usually grows in sunny, warm, dry scrub or woodland margins.

A low-growing succulent flowering plant typical of the Mediterranean region. It has creeping stems, paired turquoise-green or grey-green leaves, and small white flowers dotted with black, often growing among rocks and rural tuff walls.
A palm tree native to Mexico and parts of Central America. It produces nuts used as vegetable ivory and is also used to make cohune oil.
An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows in meadows, pastures, roadsides and waste ground, usually on alkaline ground.

A grey-green, short-lived perennial herb native to the Mediterranean region. It forms a basal leaf rosette and conspicuous blue-purple, or sometimes white, flowerheads that are popular in dried arrangements.

summary: A flowering plant whose typical variety is native to mainland Portugal, Scorzonera angustifolia is known there as narrow-leaved scorzonera. That variety is not protected under Portuguese or European Community legislation.
A hardy herbaceous perennial native to France, Spain, Portugal and Morocco. It has grey-green foliage and upright clusters of delicate white flowers with purple stamens in early summer.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Lysimachia ephemerum
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

summary: A flowering plant in the aster family, it includes the subspecies Tragopogon crocifolius subsp. crocifolius, which is native to mainland Portugal.
A tuberous herbaceous perennial native to the western Mediterranean region, including southwestern Europe and northwestern Africa. It produces dense spikes of purple flowers in spring.

A flowering shrub native to the Indian subcontinent, Tibet, Sichuan and Yunnan in China, and Myanmar. It is low, spreading and rabbit-tolerant, making it suitable for rock gardens and hedges, though it can become invasive.
Succulent flowering plant native to Mexico. It has soft, spineless leaves and, after many years, produces an unusually curved, swan-neck-like flower cluster before the flowering rosette dies.

Small fern native to northern Atlantic islands and adjacent western and southwestern Europe. It usually grows on exposed coastal clifftops and has one pointed leaf blade beside a narrow, spore-bearing spike.

An annual flowering plant native to Mediterranean Europe, it has fern-like divided leaves and flat clusters of pure white flowers. Unevenly sized florets give the blooms a memorable lace-like appearance throughout much of summer.

Wild rose native to Europe, found mostly in southern Europe and occasionally as far as the Caucasus. It resembles sweet briar but has smaller leaves, white-to-blush petals and very little scent from its flowers or leaves.
A perennial flowering plant native to Europe. It bears clear blue, five-petalled flowers after producing teardrop-shaped buds in early summer, followed by small beige ball-shaped seed heads.

sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

summary: A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows in low scrub, pastures, evergreen woodland clearings and rocky places, chiefly on limestone but also on marl, clay, alluvium and basalt.

sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A perennial herb whose native origin is not stated in the supplied sources. It survives through an egg-shaped bulb and bears loose, often one-sided clusters of narrow bell-shaped flowers in yellowish, brownish or greenish shades; the usual form flowers from February to June, while the fulvum form flowers in autumn.

summary: A scrambling shrubby vine native to central and western China. It is practically thornless, though stout shoots may carry a few prickles. Its small, fragrant white or pale-yellow flowers are among the earliest roses, usually opening in May in the Northern Hemisphere but later after cold weather.

Herbaceous perennial native to the Mediterranean area. It has waxy, channelled basal leaves and funnel-shaped white flowers from April through June; in ancient Greece its roots were a staple food, while roasted stalks and seeds were also eaten.
edibilityNote: In ancient Greece, roots were a staple food; roasted stalks and seeds were also eaten.

summary: A seaweed found widely in warm tropical waters, including parts of the Atlantic, Caribbean and Pacific. Its pale to dark-green, feather-like upright fronds rise from a shared creeping stem anchored into sandy seabeds.
A tree found from Mexico to Costa Rica in dry deciduous forests. Young trunks bear large conical thorns, while the giant fruits enclose seeds in soft white fibre formerly used to stuff mattresses.
A tree native to various parts of Latin America, it can grow tall and bears petal-free male and female flowers on the same plant. It occurs in cleared farmland, forest plains and rocky hillsides.

A fruit tree native to Central and South America. Its often twisted pods contain seeds surrounded by sweet, cottony white pulp, which is eaten raw and likened to ice cream. The seeds are reported edible only when cooked.
edibilityNote: The sweet white pulp is eaten raw; seeds are reported edible only after cooking, which destroys trypsin and chymotrypsin inhibitors.

summary: A flowering tree native from central Mexico south to Nicaragua, it bears thick thorns at the nodes of young branches. Its large, ribbed yellow-green fruit grows directly from the trunk and branches and is eaten raw, cooked, pickled or preserved.
edibilityNote: The fruit is eaten raw or cooked and is sometimes pickled or made into preserves.

summary: An evergreen tree or shrub native across the Caribbean, Mexico, Central America and northern South America. It has a dense rounded crown, strongly fragrant greenish-white flowers, and round capsules that open to reveal seeds with brightly coloured coverings.

Tree or spreading shrub endemic to New Zealand and now known only from the northern South Island. Its bark peels in long strips, and young branches tend to droop. Crowded white or pale-pink flowers can make whole hillsides look snow-covered.

A flowering subshrub endemic to Australia, false sarsaparilla grows prostrate or climbs, with leathery leaves and clusters of mostly purple flowers, though other colours sometimes occur. It can regrow from its roots after fire.

A flowering plant native to South African woodlands and Eswatini. It has arching strap-like leaves and showy red, orange or yellow flowers, sometimes with a faint sweet scent. It contains small amounts of lycorine and is poisonous.
edibilityNote: Contains small amounts of lycorine and is poisonous.

summary: A plant native to the Mediterranean basin, coastal medick is now found worldwide. It forms a partnership with a nitrogen-fixing bacterium.

Herbaceous flowering plant native to the Mediterranean region. It has bright blue flowers and blackish roots that are blue-red inside; the roots yield a red dye used since antiquity and to colour some cheeses and wines.
edibilityNote: Root dye colours some cheeses and low-quality wines; alkannin is approved as food colouring in Australia, but EU approval has been withdrawn.

summary: An orchid native around the Mediterranean from southwestern Europe and northern Africa to western Asia, its flower resembles a female sand bee and attracts males for pollination. Most subspecies are pollinated by male Andrena bees.

An evergreen perennial found throughout the Mediterranean Basin, with feathery branches of needle-like modified stems and small greenish-white to yellowish flowers. Along the Croatian coast and islands, its spring shoots are gathered for risottos or fried with scrambled eggs.
edibilityNote: Spring shoots are gathered along the Croatian coast and islands, then used in risottos or fried with scrambled eggs.

summary: A dwarf, deciduous perennial native to southwestern France and Spain, Crocus nudiflorus produces deep-purple to lilac-purple flowers in late summer or autumn. Its leaves emerge later, during winter and spring, and its underground corms spread by runners to form clumps.

A bulb-forming flowering plant whose native origin is not stated in the supplied sources. It occurs on the Iberian Peninsula and produces one to three blue-pink flowers among long, slender green leaves in autumn; its three subspecies differ in scent, leaf timing and habitat.
A subshrub native to Kenya and Tanzania. It has succulent stems that become woody near the base, year-round pink or white flowers, and mature fruit capsules that burst open.

Bulbous perennial herb regarded as native to Belize, Brazil, Colombia, Costa Rica, Honduras, Mexico, Nicaragua, Panama, Peru and Venezuela. It bears large, white, vanilla-scented flowers, and its unusually succulent seeds may be up to 90% water.

An evergreen shrub native to southern East Asia, mainland Southeast Asia and northeastern South Asia, it has glossy dark-green leaves. Its strongly fragrant white flowers bloom in summer and autumn, gradually becoming creamy yellow and waxy.
edibilityNote: Flowers are reported eaten raw, pickled or preserved in honey; in China, petals are used to scent tea.

summary: A flowering plant native to Portugal and Spain and endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. It grows in mountain meadows, sometimes on cultivated ground, and often on stony soils.

A large, semi-evergreen shrub endemic to much of southern and eastern Africa, from Kenya and Angola south. It has drooping branches, textured sage-like leaves and strongly scented flowers ranging from white and cream to mauve and purple.
An orchid native to the western Mediterranean and Macaronesia. Its stem bears two unequal leaves with heart-shaped bases, while its yellowish-green flowers resemble small bells.

A flowering plant native to Morocco, Portugal and western Spain. It typically produces just one leaf and grows in scrub clearings or beneath cork oak, oak and pine woodland, on acidic clay or sandy soils.
A flowering plant native to the Iberian Peninsula and northern Morocco, it grows in pastures, dry farmland, fallow ground and uncultivated fields, mainly on limestone-derived soils.

A small flowering plant whose subspecies petraea is native to mainland Portugal; the species occurs in the Mediterranean region. It has slender, often branched stems, divided leaves, tiny white flowers and egg-shaped fruits, and favours warm, dry, lime-rich soils in Switzerland.

summary: Bulbous perennial flowering plant native to Mediterranean Europe and North Africa. Its long, shiny leaves can conceal the short stem, while its large, lightly spicy-scented flowers are usually shades of blue; white wild forms occur occasionally.

A fern whose natural range is centred on southern South America, from Araucanía south to Cape Horn and from the Chilean coast to the Magellanic forest tree line, including nearby Argentina. It also occurs in Australia and some Pacific islands.

A poisonous perennial vine occurring in North Africa and the southern Iberian Peninsula, from Algeria to Portugal. It is usually an evergreen climber, though it rarely trails along the ground, and bears brownish-purple to reddish flowers.
Flowering plant whose subspecies Linaria aeruginea subsp. aeruginea is endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and occurs in mainland Portugal.

Perennial herb native to the southwestern Iberian Peninsula and northwestern Africa. It usually grows in moist places near waterways and bears flowers ranging from orange-red or orange-purple to greenish yellow with orange spots.

A herbaceous European lily widespread from Spain to Finland and Ukraine. It bears scentless bright yellow-orange flowers with reddish-brown dots; only the eastern variety consistently produces small aerial bulbs in the upper leaf axils.
True lily native to the Balkans and Middle East. Unlike other lilies, it forms a winter rosette that dies the following summer, followed by pure-white, strongly fragrant flowers with yellow throats.
edibilityNote: In Taiwan, its flowers and bulbs are used as food.

summary: A stem-rooting lily endemic to Taiwan and Japan's Ryukyu Islands. It bears outward-facing, trumpet-shaped white flowers with a strong fragrance. Like most true lilies, it is highly toxic to cats.
A flowering annual native to mainland Portugal. It grows on fallow ground, pasture and dry meadows, usually in acidic, sandy soil.

sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A flowering shrub native to southern Texas, Mexico, the Caribbean, Central America and South America. Its aromatic leaves are used as a cooking herb in Ethiopia and to flavour foods such as Oaxacan mole sauces.
edibilityNote: In Ethiopia it is used in spiced butter; its leaves also flavour foods including Oaxacan mole sauces.

summary: A herbaceous evergreen perennial native to East Asia, where it grows beneath shady forests in China, Japan and Korea. It forms clumps of arching, grass-like leaves, with white to violet-purple flower spikes followed by blackish berries that may persist into winter.

A fruit tree native to warm regions of Asia. Its rough red-skinned fruit has translucent, juicy flesh eaten fresh or processed into juice, preserves and dried fruit, although the fruit of L. c. philippensis is inedible.
edibilityNote: The fruit is eaten fresh or processed into juice, preserves and dried fruit; L. c. philippensis bears inedible fruit.

summary: A moss distributed across the Northern Hemisphere and Madagascar. It forms extensive, loose yellow-green to brown-green mats of sturdy, irregularly tree-shaped shoots and rarely produces spore capsules.

An orchid native to the Mediterranean and Caspian Sea regions, from Portugal and Morocco to Iran and Turkmenistan. In mainland Portugal, it grows in dry, sunny meadows and scrub clearings on limestone soils. Assessments conducted there in 2016–2019 classified it as Critically Endangered, with only two known subpopulations.
