summary: A multicellular red alga with no explicitly documented native origin, Amphiroa rigida occurs across Europe, Africa, Asia, Australia, North and South America, the Caribbean, and islands in the Indian and Pacific oceans.

An evergreen perennial native to streams and seashores of Japan. It forms loose clumps of large, round or kidney-shaped, slightly fleshy leaves. Clusters of yellow, daisy-like flowers appear in autumn and winter.

A branching shrubby plant native to Western Cape Province, South Africa. Its small, fan-shaped leaves smell of lemon and have distinctively crinkled edges; small white-to-pink flowers appear from spring to summer.
edibilityNote: The leaves are reportedly eaten in salads or used to flavour cakes and stir-fries; the source marks this section as unreferenced.

summary: A semi-woody plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. Its upright hairy stems carry dense clusters of yellow flowers, sometimes white or cream near the base, with purple veins.

A shrub recorded in the Mediterranean region and southwestern Europe, as well as Madeira and parts of North Africa. It has three-part leaves with silky undersides, yellow to orange-yellow flowers, and pods densely covered in glandular bumps.

Flowering plant native to the Iberian Peninsula, where the typical subspecies is endemic; subsp. fontiqueri is reported as endemic to mainland Portugal. Both subspecies occur in mainland Portugal and are not protected under Portuguese or European Community law.

An evergreen herb endemic to the northwestern Iberian Peninsula. It is upright and spiny, with persistent bluish-green leaves and a large cylindrical terminal flower head accompanied by much smaller side heads.

A tropical tree native to the Greater Sunda Islands, Malay Peninsula, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands. Its crushed leaves are aromatic, and its edible bell-shaped berries have thin skin and white, spongy flesh; they are eaten fresh and used in salads, sautéed dishes, and pickles.
edibilityNote: The edible fruit is eaten fresh, in salads and lightly sautéed dishes, and made into pickles in Indian Ocean island cuisines.

summary: A short-lived perennial herb endemic to Spain’s Sierra Nevada, with some reports from the nearby Sierra de Gádor. In the narrow sense, it has multiple flowering stems, narrow hairy grey-green leaves and yellow flowers; its fruits may be upright or drooping.

A herb whose native origin is not stated, it is found mainly in the Mediterranean region, especially Spain, France and Italy, in dry meadows. It has a small underground bulb, two threadlike leaves and usually no more than four yellow, star-shaped flowers. It flowers in February and early March.

Rare tufted perennial flowering plant with no explicitly stated native origin; it is found in mountainous southern Europe and southwest Asia, and was first noted in Ireland’s Caha Mountains in 1964. Its wiry stems rise from a woody base, bearing needle-like, often side-curving leaves and white five-petalled flowers from late spring through summer.

A flowering plant endemic to mainland Portugal, Murbeckiella boryi belongs to the mustard family. It is protected under Portuguese or European legislation, including Annex V of the Habitats Directive.

A trailing, mat-forming plant recorded in parts of Spain and southern France. Its small, deeply divided leaves are sticky with glandular hairs, sun-exposed plants may turn reddish, and rounded white flowers appear in spring and summer.

A saxifrage native to Ireland, Portugal and Spain. It forms a rosette of elongated succulent leaves around an upright, leafless flowering stem and grows among acidic rocks in humus-rich alpine habitats. It is native to Ireland but absent from Great Britain.

A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, Scrophularia herminii occurs in mainland Portugal. It is protected under Portuguese or European Community legislation, including Annex V of the Habitats Directive.

Flowering plant of unstated native origin, recorded across many mountain systems of the northern Iberian Peninsula. It grows in wild mountain grasslands, especially stony places. The subspecies caespitosus is endemic to Portugal’s Serra da Estrela and is legally protected.
A flowering plant endemic to central mainland Portugal. It grows in cracks and dry rocky slopes on acidic mountain ridges, and its population is considered stable and of Least Concern.

A tree endemic to southeastern Australia. It has thick, rough, stringy bark on its trunk and larger branches but smooth bark on thinner branches, along with curved adult leaves, white flowers and woody cup- or barrel-shaped fruit.

A small to medium flowering tree native to Tasmanian woodlands, cider gum has mostly smooth bark, bluish-green leaves and white flowers in groups of three. Tasmanian Aboriginal people used its sap to make a fermented beverage called way-a-linah.
edibilityNote: Tasmanian Aboriginal people used the tree's sap to produce the fermented beverage way-a-linah.

summary: Flowering sedge native to Africa, Australasia, Europe and the Pacific islands. It is commonly known as floating club-rush or floating scirpus.

A perennial rush native to southern Australia, New Zealand, Norfolk Island and Lord Howe Island. It forms vigorous tufts, bears many straw-coloured flowers and usually grows in periodically flooded, nutrient-poor soils around fresh or brackish waterways.

Ground-growing fern native only to Australia, including southeastern mainland regions and Tasmania. Rows of spore clusters line its fronds, which can carry buds that grow into small plants. As those buds become heavier, the fronds sag until they can root in the soil.

A tree endemic to southeastern Australia. It has thick, rough reddish-brown to black bark, with flower buds usually grouped in threes, white or pale pink flowers, and woody cylindrical or rounded fruit.

An erect flowering shrub native to continental Europe, Scandinavia, the Black Sea region, Iran, Afghanistan and Pakistan. It is a pioneer of recently scoured riverbanks in mountainous areas and may have white, cream or pink flowers.
A perennial herb native to eastern Australia and New Zealand, often growing beside shady streams.
A tall, dense shrub or occasional tree native to southeastern Australia. Its papery bark and small, prolific flower heads distinguish it from similar species, and it often grows in swampy areas.
edibilityNote: Aboriginal people used nectar from the flowers to make sweet drinks.

summary: A shrub or small tree endemic to coastal Australia, it grows on dunes and cliffs and tolerates salt well. Its purple to black fruit is edible and suitable for jams and jellies.
edibilityNote: The purple fruit is eaten and used to make jams and jellies.

summary: A large shrub or small weeping tree native to southeastern Australia. It has rough grey fibrous bark, dense foliage with narrow hook-tipped leaves, and cylindrical clusters of pale flowers followed by woody capsules.

A shrub endemic to the Azores, it occurs on every island except Corvo and Graciosa. Its pointed, serrated leaves may turn reddish-yellow in autumn, while its clustered pinkish-white flowers are followed by fleshy, cylindrical black fruit.
A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and Madeira; Madeira is explicitly reported as native, while the Azores population is introduced.

Evergreen perennial native to mountainous southwestern Europe, from the Pyrenees to Portugal. It forms dense clumps of white or near-white flowers from mid to late spring and prefers moist, well-drained sandy soil.
A flowering plant with no native origin supplied at species level. Its variety velucensis is documented as native to mainland Portugal.

sources.title: Paronychia polygonifolia (Vill.) DC.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A flowering plant native to the high mountains of the Iberian Peninsula and southern France, Silene ciliata occurs in Portugal only in Serra da Estrela, in meadows on granite sand. Portugal’s 2020 mainland Red List assessed it as Endangered, with only two identified locations and continuing habitat decline.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Silene ciliata
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

summary: An upright shrub endemic to the Canary Islands, it has oblong leaves and terminal clusters of numerous white flowers. Flowering lasts from late winter to early summer.

A perennial herb or shrub found in southern and eastern Europe, Turkey, the Caucasus and Algeria. It has upright ochre-orange stems that are mostly leafless and scarred, with grey-green leaves clustered near their tips and flower heads.

A perennial sedge native to Eurasia, Africa and Australia, growing in wet ground and shallow water. It forms dense clumps of three-angled stems, with bladeless leaf sheaths and compact heads of cone-shaped flower spikes beside a stiff, stem-like bract.
Flowering grass with two subspecies documented as native in Portugal: subsp. farctus in mainland Portugal, and subsp. boreo-atlanticus in mainland Portugal and Madeira.

A succulent shrub or small tree of unspecified native origin, it is widespread in eastern South Africa and Eswatini and also abundant in the drier southern Cape. It commonly has reddish stems and green leaves. In Southern Africa it is commonly eaten, usually in salad or soup, but should not be confused with the mildly toxic jade plant.
edibilityNote: Commonly eaten in Southern Africa, usually in salad or soup; it should not be confused with the mildly toxic jade plant.

summary: A small banana species native to Southeast Asia, including Bangladesh, Burma and India, flowering banana has green foliage tinged with pink. It bears pink flowers and small dark pink or crimson, seeded, inedible fruit, while its brightly coloured bracts make it a memorable ornamental.
edibilityNote: The male bud may be cooked or used in salads; the seeded fruit is inedible.

summary: Green seaweed native to the northeastern Atlantic from Ireland south to the Azores and Cape Verde. Its highly branched fronds feel spongy and felt-like and bear colourless hairs visible underwater; it grows on exposed rocks in deep pools on the lower shore.

A dwarf, aromatic groundcover shrub native to oceanic parts of northwestern Portugal and Spain, the Azores and Madeira. It forms mats of narrow, smooth leaves and bears flattened heads of rose, lilac or white flowers from late spring into summer.

A sprawling perennial herb native to the western Mediterranean, from southwestern France through the Iberian Peninsula to the Azores, Morocco and Algeria. It grows in damp ground or water and overwinters underwater in its native habitat. In Portugal, the whole plant, fresh or dried, is added to stews, salads, soups, cheeses and sauces, and used in liqueur infusions.
edibilityNote: In Portugal, the whole plant is used fresh or dried in savoury foods and in liqueur infusions.

summary: A flowering plant native to southern Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay and Argentina, giant sea holly has very long, narrow leaves resembling pampas grass. Introduced to Portugal, it has been legally classified there as invasive since 1999 and has established in damp areas around the Tagus and Mondego river basins.

A perennial flowering shrub endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and Aquitaine, with an Azorean subspecies that may be a separate species. Male and female flowers usually grow on separate plants, although some southwestern Iberian plants also bear bisexual flower clusters whose fruit tends to be underdeveloped. Its ripe, white, tough-skinned fruits are edible, mildly acidic and lemony; people in Iberia have eaten the berries since at least the Middle Ages.
edibilityNote: Ripe white fruits are edible, mildly acidic and lemony; the berries have been consumed in Iberia since at least the Middle Ages.

summary: Small pinkish seaweed recorded from the Faroe Islands and Norway to the Mediterranean, including waters around Britain and Ireland. It forms firmly attached, flat lobed crusts that may become knobbly or bleached, commonly in shallow pools and beneath cover down to 8 metres.
A herbaceous plant native to the Caribbean.
A flowering plant whose subspecies Silene portensis subsp. portensis is native to mainland Portugal.

A medium-sized red marine alga whose native origin is not specified; it occurs from Norway and the Faroes to Senegal, the Mediterranean and the Canary Islands. Its flattened branches alternate between long and short forms, with curved side branches creating a comb-like pattern.

A small, uncommon seaweed found around Great Britain and Ireland, the Azores, and the Atlantic coast from Massachusetts to Virginia, Gymnogongrus griffithsiae grows in lower-shore rock pools and just below the shore. It is dark purplish brown, with erect, stiff fronds that fork in one plane and have slightly flattened tips.

Small red marine alga of unstated native origin, recorded around the British Isles and from Norway and the Mediterranean to the Indian and Pacific oceans. It grows in shaded upper-shore sites as dark brown, creeping, moss-like branches visibly pinched at intervals.
A multicellular red marine alga with no stated native origin, found across Europe, Africa, Asia and Australia, as well as islands in the Pacific, Indian and Atlantic oceans.

A red alga with no specific native origin stated, Amphiroa beauvoisii is widely distributed, mainly in tropical and subtropical waters. It attaches to intertidal rocks by a calcified base and produces flat, branching, fan-like growth whose form varies with location.
Perennial herb native to the mountains of Southern Europe, with a fuzzy woody stem and paired leaves. Its generally violet flowers appear between May and August depending on altitude.
edibilityNote: The plant can be brewed and served as tea.

summary: A wild banana plant originally from Assam and the eastern Himalayas. It bears fuzzy pink fruits on upright flower stalks, and the ripe fruits peel themselves back. Their soft, sweet flesh is edible, but the tough seeds can chip a tooth.
edibilityNote: The soft, sweet fruit flesh can be eaten, but the tough seeds can chip a tooth.

summary: A bulbous perennial native to South Africa’s Eastern Cape Province, silver squill is often cultivated and grows well with minimal care.
Flowering plant endemic to Brazil. Its centre turns red shortly before flowering, creating its characteristic blushing appearance.
Evergreen flowering climber native to Colombia, with red stems and large heart-shaped leaves. Its deep-red, fragrant flower structures appear in summer and autumn.
edibilityNote: All parts are toxic because they contain calcium oxalate and should be kept away from young children.

summary: Wetland plant native to Japan, Korea and eastern Asia. Its long, narrow, slightly curved leaves grow in very moist soil or partly or fully submerged, while its rhizomes can spread aggressively into dense groundcover.

A hornwort whose native origin is not stated. It grows in moist soil and waterways, forming a nearly flat, dark green, slightly glossy body. When numerous, its slender green spore capsules resemble tufts of grass.

A seaweed with no native origin specified, Ulva clathrata occurs across parts of Europe, Asia, Africa and the Americas, as well as several oceans, gulfs and seas. It is light green and forms thin, cylindrical threads.
A green seaweed found worldwide, Flexuous Gutweed is a large, tubular and highly variable alga. Its branches have cells arranged lengthwise and sometimes crosswise.

A tree-like cactus from southern South America, probably including Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay and Argentina. Its branching, segmented stems are usually spineless, while large white flowers open on summer nights and are followed by red-to-yellow fruits with white pulp.
edibilityNote: In Rio Grande do Sul, the fruits are appreciated by local people.

summary: Small flowering tree native to the Caribbean, including Jamaica, Hispaniola, Puerto Rico, and the Leeward and Windward Islands. Its showy flowers make it a popular ornamental.

Fast-growing perennial vine endemic to Rio de Janeiro state in Brazil. Its long woody stems twine around supports, while pink-red funnel-shaped flowers appear over a long period from spring into autumn.

Perennial plant native to several countries in southern South America. Purple cultivars have three-part leaves that fold down at night, when disturbed or in harsh sunlight; white or pale pink flowers also close at night.
edibilityNote: Leaves and flowers are edible in moderation, but large quantities may cause toxicity from soluble calcium oxalates.

summary: A tender trailing perennial native to southern Africa, it has aromatic, glossy, rounded leaves that sometimes show deep purple centres and undersides. White, pale violet or pale pink flowers may appear sporadically year-round, especially in spring and late autumn.
Fruit tree native to the Amazon rainforest in Brazil, Colombia, Peru and Ecuador. It bears pale green fruits that turn bright yellow when ripe, with juicy, aromatic and strongly acidic pulp.
edibilityNote: The acidic fruit is eaten fresh, preferably with sugar, or processed into juices, nectars, marmalades, ice creams and other foods.

summary: Creeping evergreen flowering perennial native to rainforests of Colombia, Peru, Bolivia, Ecuador and northern Brazil. Its dark green leaves are marked by strongly contrasting veins, from white to deep pink or red, while its stems are lightly fuzzy and its flowers small and pale.

A perennial flowering plant native to eastern Brazil's Atlantic Forest, northeastern Argentina and Paraguay. It is cultivated as a decorative potted or landscape feature plant in warm temperate and subtropical climates.
Herbaceous plant native to Venezuela, Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador and Peru. It has been introduced to places including Hawaii and the Galápagos Islands.

A rhizomatous flowering plant native to the eastern Himalayas from southern Bhutan to northern Myanmar. It is prized for dark leaves marked with prominent silvery-grey bands and is usually grown for foliage rather than flowers.

Evergreen tree endemic to New Zealand. Its leaves usually have seven sharply toothed leaflets, with young leaves shiny and purplish underneath. Māori used its timber to make fire by friction and its fruit juice as a dye.

Soft-wooded shrub native to eastern Australia; in New Zealand it is reported as indigenous, though some authorities consider it introduced. It has blue-purple flowers and orange-red to scarlet fruit. Ripe berries were traditional Māori food and were stewed or made into pies and jam by early European settlers; using leaves in hāngī is now discouraged because they contain poisonous alkaloids.
edibilityNote: Ripe berries were traditional Māori food and early settlers stewed them or made pies and jam; leaf use in hāngī is now discouraged.

summary: A climbing cactus native to Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Nicaragua, Panama, Peru, Trinidad and Tobago, and Venezuela, yellow dragonfruit has exceptionally large night-blooming flowers. Its spiny yellow fruit has edible white flesh with a pleasant, mildly sweet flavour; hybrids may have differently coloured skin or flesh.
edibilityNote: The fruit’s white interior is edible and mildly sweet; hybrid fruit may have pink flesh.

summary: Salt-tolerant flowering plant native to Portugal. It grows in estuary and lagoon salt marshes, with fleshy stems and scale-like leaves that are green in spring and summer but reddish in autumn.

A woody evergreen vine native to southern tropical India, it bears long hanging clusters of strongly curved flowers. The flowers are rich yellow with maroon to brownish-red tips and appear from spring to autumn.

A densely branching flowering subshrub found from Mediterranean Europe and northern and central Africa through western Asia, Cressa cretica also occurs in Southeast Asia and Australia, where its native status is unclear. It has silky-haired leaves and white flowers and grows in salty, seasonally wet places.
A perennial herb endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and North Africa. It grows on rocky ground and slopes, with a woody base, profusely branching stems and broadly arrow-shaped leaves.

A fast-growing tropical tree native to tropical South America. Its edible fruit ripens from green to yellow and has a soft-spined surface that bruises and blackens easily, contributing to a shelf life of under a week. The very soft, sweet pulp is usually eaten fresh, though it is also cooked and made into wine in Brazil.
edibilityNote: The sweet fruit pulp is usually eaten fresh; chefs sometimes cook it, and it has been made into wine in Brazil.

summary: A perennial shrub or subshrub native to South America, lemon verbena has glossy, pointed leaves that release a strong lemon scent when bruised. Its leaves flavour foods and drinks, including fish, poultry, jams and herbal tea, and are also used to flavour liqueurs.
edibilityNote: Leaves are used to flavour cooked dishes, marinades, dressings, jams, puddings, yogurt and beverages, and to make herbal tea and flavour liqueurs.

summary: An aromatic, spiny deciduous shrub or small tree native to Japan and Korea; its natural range also includes mainland China. Its scarlet berries burst open in autumn to scatter black seeds. Young leaves and ground or prepared fruits are used as flavorings in Japanese and Korean cooking.
edibilityNote: Mature fruits are ground as spice; immature berries are blanched, salted or simmered, while young leaves, shoots and male flowers are eaten in Japan and Korea.

summary: A stemless evergreen shrub native to south-central and southeastern North America. Its sharply pointed, sword-like leaves often fold under their own weight, and tall summer flower clusters rise above them with creamy white, bell-shaped blooms.

A deciduous tree native to tropical Southeast Asia and northern Australasia, it produces masses of golden summer flowers. Its pods change from red to black as they ripen, and the tree is widely planted as an ornamental.

A creeping wetland perennial native to Western and Central Europe, creeping marshwort is rare throughout its range. Its trailing stems root at their joints and can form mats where flooding, mowing or grazing keeps taller vegetation in check.
edibilityNote: Its leaves taste mild and parsley-like, but the source only speculates about edibility and documents no clear human food use.

summary: A low-growing, hairless perennial flowering plant native to western Europe, found in ditches, streams, and fresh or brackish wetlands. Its hollow stems root where nodes touch the ground, and crushed leaves smell of carrot. Traditionally harvested in several Mediterranean countries, its young leaves and tender shoots are eaten raw, boiled, or as a condiment, though it can be confused with allegedly poisonous lesser water parsnip.
edibilityNote: Young leaves and tender shoots are traditionally eaten in several Mediterranean countries, raw in salads, boiled, or used as a condiment.

summary: A small marine red alga recorded from Great Britain and Ireland south to Portugal and the Mediterranean. Its flattened, fan-shaped fronds grow from a disc-like anchor and divide into blades with rounded tips.

Flowering herbaceous perennial native to southern China, the Himalayas, India and Indochina. It grows along forest edges and in mountain grasslands, producing flowers from red and orange to almost yellow.

A perennial flowering herb native mainly to Missouri and Arkansas, with additional populations in Louisiana and Illinois, Drummond's goldenrod spreads through underground stems. A single plant can bear 200 or more small yellow flower heads in a large, sometimes drooping, branched display.

A small bulb-growing species of garlic native to the Mediterranean region, Allium chamaemoly has an extremely short or absent flower stalk, so its flowers appear at ground level. Its white flowers usually have a purple stripe, while its flat, grass-like leaves often bear long white hairs.

summary: A bulb-forming perennial wild onion native to southern Iberia, the Balearic Islands, Sicily and North Africa; it might be introduced in the Azores. Its narrow leaves bear conspicuous long white hairs, and its white flowers have yellow anthers.

A tall herbaceous perennial of unstated native origin, giant fennel has hollow stalks and produces resin from its root or lower stalk. Its young stems and flower clusters were eaten in ancient Rome and remain eaten in Morocco, though culinary use can cause poisoning.
edibilityNote: Young stems and inflorescences were eaten in ancient Rome and remain eaten in Morocco; poisoning can occur, and Sardinia has poisonous and non-poisonous chemotypes.

summary: A Mediterranean-endemic perennial found in dry grassland, rocky places, roadsides and waste ground. Its many rigid, twisting stems form a tangled bush, while a large fleshy root is wrapped near the top in brown fibres left by old leaves.

Clump-forming, fleshy-leaved plant endemic to South Africa's Eastern Cape Province. Its small light-green rosettes usually have slightly bristly leaf margins and transparent streaks or tips; in the wild, the plant is mostly buried in sand with only these tips showing.
A flowering-plant species native to mainland Portugal and introduced in the Azores.

An aromatic perennial of the western Mediterranean and southern Atlantic coast of the Iberian Peninsula. It grows on coastal sand, dunes and rocky shores, bearing solitary daisy-like flower heads with white rays and yellow centres.

sources.title: Anthemis maritima L.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A herbaceous perennial native to the Mediterranean. Its nearly leafless upright stalks carry yellow flower heads ringed by thorny bracts, including stiff golden inner bracts, and it flowers from June through August.
A low, trailing succulent endemic to New Zealand. Its fleshy, three-sided leaves and white-to-deep-pink daisy-like flowers distinguish it on cliffs, gravel beaches, salt meadows and estuaries.
edibilityNote: European settlers ate its bland, fleshy capsules and pickled its leaves.

summary: A tree fern native to New Zealand.

A deciduous flowering climber native to mountainous Asia from Afghanistan to Taiwan. In late spring it produces masses of scented white or pink flowers for about four weeks, each with four petals and prominent yellow anthers.

A perennial plant distributed along the southern Atlantic coast of the Iberian Peninsula and through the western Mediterranean to Italy. It grows in sand, dunes and pine scrub, with purple flower heads surrounded by scales bearing hooked reddish-brown spines.

sources.title: Centaurea sphaerocephala L.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A culinary herb in the buckwheat family, French sorrel has a tart, slightly lemony taste from oxalic acid and may become bitter later in the season. It is eaten in salads, soups and sauces, especially sauces for fish.
edibilityNote: Used as a culinary herb in salads, soups and sauces, especially with fish; tart from oxalic acid and sometimes bitter later in the season.

summary: A low woody flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and occurring across southwestern Europe and North Africa. It grows in scrub and uncultivated ground, flowering from May to July.

A herb found only on the Iberian Peninsula, mainly at inland sites in Spain and a small neighbouring area of Portugal. Its recognised subspecies and varieties are largely geographically separate, and the plant blooms from April to October in habitats including woodland edges, scrub and roadsides.
An ascending legume recorded in the Iberian Peninsula and northern Morocco. It has hairy stems, purple-and-white flowers and very hairy pods edged with several spines.

A rhizomatous perennial herb native to temperate Europe. It grows in wet places and bears solitary white flowers tinged with yellow and purple. All parts are poisonous, and some historical medicinal use resulted in fatal poisoning.
edibilityNote: All parts are poisonous; historical medicinal use caused some fatal poisonings, and the plant is no longer used because of the poisoning risk.

summary: A flowering rush native to northwestern Africa, many Mediterranean islands, warmer parts of southern, central and eastern Europe, and western Asia, sand rush favours wet, nutrient-poor rock, sand or clay soils. It often occurs in clay pits, old brickyards and along roads.

A sedge native in Wallonia, sweet galingale is also widespread across Africa, southern Europe, the Indian subcontinent and western Asia. It has creeping underground stems and upright triangular stalks, and grows in shallow water or damp ground such as pond edges. Its thick yellowish underground stems are traditionally harvested to distil sweet-scented oil for perfume.

An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It inhabits wet meadows, marshes and temporarily flooded pasture around lagoons, springs and permanent waterways, particularly on siliceous ground.

A flowering plant in the daisy family, Leucanthemopsis pulverulenta includes a subspecies endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. This subspecies occurs in mainland Portugal and is not protected under Portuguese or European Community legislation.

An annual herb occurring across southern Europe, North Africa and parts of Asia. It may grow upright or trail along the ground, with usually yellow flowers and hairy, glandular pods containing several brown seeds.

sources.title: Ononis viscosa L.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: Annual flowering plant native to the Palearctic, from the western Mediterranean to Central Asia. It grows in sandy, well-drained ground, particularly coastal and desert dunes.
A perennial, thistle-like plant occurring in southern Europe and North Africa. It has spiny leaves that partly dry by flowering time and solitary flower heads filled with yellow flowers.

A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. Within Portugal it is characteristic of major-river floodplains, occurs at only three known locations along the Douro and Tagus, and was assessed as Endangered with an estimated population of about 500 mature plants.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Andryala ragusina
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

summary: An annual lupine endemic to the western half of the Iberian Peninsula. Its pinkish-blue flowers form neat rings along a spike, while its leaves have several leaflets radiating from one point. The whole plant feels soft and has a particularly strong smell.

A herbaceous plant endemic to Mediterranean areas of southwestern Europe, Spanish birthwort occurs from the Iberian Peninsula through southern France to Corsica and Sardinia. It inhabits rocky places, fallows and clearings among heaths, scrub or holm oak groves.
A perennial plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, it has several smooth or nearly smooth stems and narrow leaves. It grows in open scrub and uncultivated ground, usually on dry, often stony soils.
A flowering plant whose nominate subspecies, Linaria viscosa subsp. viscosa, is endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and occurs in mainland Portugal.
An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows in meadows, pasture, fallow and uncultivated land, often on sandy soils.

An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It occurs in open grassland, scrub clearings, olive groves, fields, roadsides and embankments. Possible identification features needing confirmation include persistent sepals and two distinct kinds of hairs on the fruits.

A biennial rose-family plant recorded around the Mediterranean and on the Iberian Peninsula. Its club-shaped flower heads place female flowers at the top and bisexual flowers below, while its large, roughly pyramidal or egg-shaped fruit has conspicuous warts.
A flowering grass native to Europe, North Africa and temperate Asia. It is a tufted perennial with spreading underground stems, stiff flat leaves and a narrow flower cluster.
A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. In Portugal it grows in shady, waterside herb communities beneath riverside woodland, often under alder trees.
An annual thistle found across the Mediterranean region, it occurs mainly in non-alpine, non-saline wetlands and grasslands. It is spiny and slender, with simple broad leaves.
A hardy, clump-forming perennial native to the Iberian Peninsula and the Atlas Mountains of Morocco and Algeria. It grows on rocky slopes, and its numerous stems were formerly used to make brooms.
Flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula in Spain and Portugal. It grows up to four metres tall and bears very small leaves.
A flowering grass whose album and erianthum varieties are native to mainland Portugal. No habitat information is supplied.

Annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and distributed across the Mediterranean region. It grows on stony, alkaline soils around cliffs, scree and roadsides. A 2020 mainland Portuguese assessment classified its small, scattered national population as Vulnerable.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Arabis verna
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

summary: An annual herb with no native origin stated in the supplied information. It is self-supporting and has simple, broad leaves.
A shrubby flowering plant of unstated native origin. It belongs to a group of Cistus species with white or whitish-pink flowers.

A rush with no native origin stated, it has sharp-looking flowers in warm brown and maroon shades, appearing from July to September. Its hollow, smooth leaves have cross-walls that make them feel jointed.

An evergreen shrub native to southern Europe, including the western Iberian Peninsula, and northwestern Africa, including Morocco. It has tiny needle-like leaves and pink to purple bell-shaped flowers in late spring.
A flowering plant whose subspecies Veronica anagalloides subsp. anagalloides is native to mainland Portugal.

A perennial herb found from European mountain ranges into western, central and southern Asia, it has lilac flowers from July through October. It typically grows in rocky, lime-rich places, woodland edges and subalpine meadows, but also occurs beside marshes and lakes.

An evergreen shrub or small tree of Mediterranean forests, growing wild in Algeria, Morocco, Sardinia and Spain. Its glossy oval leaves are larger than those of common boxwood and may develop reddish or yellowish colouring.

A cinquefoil native to France and the northern half of the Iberian Peninsula, it grows in rocky places, banks, meadows and edges. In Portugal, the 2020 assessment classified it as Endangered, with fewer than 1,000 mature plants concentrated in one declining subpopulation.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Potentilla montana
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

summary: A branching subshrub of Eurasia, it is widespread from Portugal to Pakistan. Its deeply lobed basal leaves contrast with the narrow, unlobed stem leaves, while its flower heads have four or five yellow ray flowers but no disc flowers.

A deciduous tree native to Europe, it has rough, scaly bark and birch-like, double-toothed leaves. Its nuts hang in clusters, each enclosed in a bladder-like covering, while its very hard wood was historically used for plane soles, cogs and gears.

An evergreen, woolly perennial subshrub naturally found on coasts from Western Europe and the Mediterranean to parts of the Black Sea and Caucasus, cottonweed forms dense silver-white mounds. Its small fleshy leaves smell strongly aromatic when bruised, while its clustered yellow flower heads lack the usual daisy-like outer petals.

A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows on dry, stony roadsides, path banks and scrub edges, sometimes in disturbed places; current Portuguese records are confined to the Algarve, where known populations are small.

sources.title: Plumbago europaea L.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A perennial herb native to mainland Portugal. Its showy flowers occur among shaded limestone rocks, cliffs and scree, and it is very rare in concentrated populations in west-central Portugal's limestone hills.

A flowering plant native to South Africa, including the Northern Cape, Eastern Cape and Free State. This highly variable species has velvety flowers of various shapes and colours, produced intermittently in late summer and autumn. The flowers smell of carrion and attract flies.

A succulent tree native to dry areas of southern Africa, the candelabra tree has thick, ridged green stems and small greenish-yellow flowers. Its milky latex is extremely poisonous and can cause blindness, severe skin irritation or poisoning if swallowed.
edibilityNote: The milky latex is extremely poisonous and can poison humans and animals when ingested.

summary: A deciduous shrub or small tree indigenous to southern Africa. Its purple, mauve, pink or rarely white flowers form an unusual double-star shape, followed by four-lobed reddish-brown fruits that remain after ripening. The fruits are locally eaten raw, fermented with traditional beer or mixed with goat’s milk to make berry yoghurt.
edibilityNote: Fruits are locally eaten raw, fermented with traditional beer, or mixed with goat’s milk to make berry yoghurt.

summary: A hardy perennial present in northern Africa and southern Europe, it has long stems with divided, fern-like leaves. White or pale lemon flowers appear from July to November.

A sedge native to Mediterranean coasts and nearby areas, capitate galingale grows in coastal sands and spreads through scaly underground roots. Its thick blue-grey leaves are U-shaped, while its flowers form a single crowded head.
Rosette-forming succulent perennial native to the Alps, Apennines and Carpathians of Europe. Its furry central rosettes resemble spider webs, and raised stems bear pink flowers in July.

A small annual spurge native to southern and western Europe, northern Africa and southwestern Asia, usually growing on coastal sand and shingle. It lies low against the ground and has fleshy grey-green leaves with reddish-purple veins. At its northern range edge in England, it was always rare and is now extinct.

An annual climbing herb whose native origin is not supplied. It has broad leaves and is associated with freshwater habitats; in Portugal it also grows along field edges, paths, banks and waterways, favouring somewhat shady or moist places.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal but introduced in the Azores and Madeira. It grows in moist meadows, hedges, agricultural floodplains and traditional orchards.

A flowering plant whose mollis and reclinata subspecies are native to mainland Portugal. It bears hanging pink flowers and hairy pods; both subspecies grow in annual grasslands on rocks and stony ground, generally over alkaline material.

sources.title: Ononis reclinata L.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and Madeira but introduced in the Azores. It has yellow flowers and strongly flattened, segmented pods, and grows in annual grasslands, open woodlands, fallow ground and pastures, usually on silica-rich ground.

sources.title: Ornithopus compressus L.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A flowering plant native to the Canary Islands, Mediterranean and Middle East as far east as Iran, cupped clover has been introduced to Australia as forage. Three cultivars have been developed there.

A usually annual herb of Mediterranean distribution, though its native origin is not explicitly supplied. Its low or climbing stems bear leaves ending in simple tendrils and small pale-purple or pale-blue flowers, usually singly or in small groups; in Portugal it inhabits moist meadows, field grasslands and woodland or scrub edges.

sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A tall tree native only to north-eastern Australia, with smooth bark ranging from white to pink or coppery tones. Its narrow, glossy leaves are often lemon-scented when crushed, and its flowers are white.

An aquatic perennial native to northern and eastern Australia, and possibly New Guinea, the blue waterlily has large floating leaves and blue or lilac flowers that fade almost white. After fertilisation, its fruit is drawn underwater to ripen. Indigenous Australians traditionally ate roasted tubers, raw peeled stalks and flower buds, and roasted seeds or seed flour.
edibilityNote: Indigenous Australians ate roasted tubers, raw peeled stalks and flower buds, and seeds roasted or pounded into flour.

summary: A slender tree endemic to eastern Australia. Its drooping branchlets bear leaves reduced to tiny scales, while its warty, barrel-shaped cones contain brown winged seeds.
A perennial plant native to Europe, North Africa and western Asia. One specimen was recorded as collected at Salem, Oregon, in 1910.

Aquatic annual or perennial native to Europe, southwestern Asia and northern Africa. It has broad, rounded floating leaves and finely divided, thread-like submerged leaves. Its flowers are white with yellow centres.

A perennial aquatic flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and distributed in Europe. It lives submerged in shallow, temperate rivers and streams, with brush-like underwater leaves and usually no floating leaves.

sources.title: Ranunculus penicillatus (Dumort.) Bab.
sources.attribution: Info Flora, plazi (2021). Info Flora Schweiz - Ranunculaceae. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/kxyxpm accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A flowering herb found mainly in Europe, with reports extending to Morocco and Turkey, though its range is uncertain. It grows in shallow water or exposed mud and may carry both thread-like submerged leaves and flat, deeply three-lobed surface leaves. Its small white flowers have a yellow patch near the base.
A flowering water plant native to mainland Portugal. It inhabits cold, very shallow, nutrient-poor standing water or very slow streams, including bogs, springs, ponds and lagoons.

Dwarf amphibious annual or perennial herb of unstated native origin. It grows directly in water or very damp places, often forming dense stands, with rounded leaves along the stem and a flower-like leaf bundle at the top. Broken fragments can develop into new plants.

An aquatic perennial restricted to Europe, Turkey and extreme North Africa, it inhabits shallow, peaty, calcium-rich waters. Its thin, translucent, net-veined leaves are often reddish or brownish and may sit just below the surface, creating a distinctive drowned appearance.

sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

summary: An aquatic perennial native to the western Palearctic and Africa, hairlike pondweed grows mainly in standing or slow-flowing water. It survives winter as numerous resting bodies and has stiff, very narrow submerged leaves but no floating leaves.

A succulent subshrub endemic to east-central Madagascar, the panda plant has thick, velvety silver-green leaves edged or spotted with dark brown to rusty red. In its natural habitat it flowers from March to June, but indoor plants rarely bloom.
edibilityNote: Mildly toxic to humans if ingested.

summary: A bulbous daffodil native to the southwest Iberian Peninsula and northwest Africa. Unlike other daffodils, its central floral cup is almost completely absent. A 2020 mainland Portugal assessment classified it as Critically Endangered, with only two known subpopulations there.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Narcissus cavanillesii
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

summary: A tropical tree native to southeastern Brazil. It bears yellow flowers intermittently throughout the year and long, four-sided seedpods that rattle; its glossy leaflets form thin green foliage.
edibilityNote: The seeds and other unspecified plant parts are poisonous if eaten.

summary: A bushy perennial flowering shrub native to parts of the Mediterranean and Middle East. Its golden-yellow flowers have conspicuously long stamens, and its leaves usually produce a goat-like smell, though one subspecies lacks it.

An evergreen flowering climber native to southern southwestern mainland Portugal. It climbs using its leaf stalks and has variable leaves. Its whitish, bell-shaped flowers have a honey-like fragrance and appear from October to December.

sources.title: Clematis cirrhosa L.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: An evergreen or semi-evergreen ground fern native to New Zealand, the Chatham Islands, several New Zealand subantarctic islands and Australia’s Macquarie Island, prickly shield fern has an erect, scaly underground stem that may form a short trunk. Round spore clusters occur beneath its fronds.
A grass-like herb native to southern Europe, Lebanon and Syria.

Deciduous climbing plant native to southern Europe and northern Africa. It forms dense tangles covered with white flowers during warmer months; newly opened flowers have a strong sweet-almond fragrance.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It grows chiefly on coastal sands, especially primary and secondary dunes, and occurs less often on coastal rocks.

sources.title: Crucianella maritima L.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: An erect perennial native to the Mediterranean region from Portugal and Morocco to Greece, extending north into Germany. It has narrow leaves arranged in rings around the stem and a large terminal cluster of many small white to cream flowers.

A small perennial shrub with no explicitly stated native origin, Osyris alba is widespread across the Mediterranean basin, western Asia and North Africa. It is semiparasitic, with leaves produced in winter but almost entirely absent in summer, and bears small red, fleshy fruits.
Annual plant native to Southern Europe and parts of the Middle East and Northwest Africa. It flowers from May to June and grows in dry, sunny grasslands, often on carbonate ground.
Flowering plant native to mainland Portugal, where it is assessed as Regionally Extinct. It was collected at Foz Tua in July 1905 but has not been observed there since, despite repeated searches.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Plantago sempervirens
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

summary: A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. Its narrow, grasslike leaves and several long-stalked yellow flowers distinguish it; it grows in rocky meadows and rock cracks, particularly on limestone.

sources.title: Ranunculus gramineus L.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: An erect, deciduous shrub found in central and southern Europe, particularly in woods, scrub and rocky slopes. Its many smooth, thorny branches carry clustered leaves, and it produces greenish fruits with two or three stones.

A stemless flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It spreads through short, mostly underground runners and bears fragrant pale-violet flowers with dark lines and white centres; occasional plants in Portugal have white flowers.

sources.title: Viola suavis M.Bieb.
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A semi-evergreen trailing perennial native to the Dinaric Alps in the former Yugoslavia. It has lavender-blue, star-shaped flowers from mid-spring to early autumn and readily seeds into cracks in walls and paving. Its leaves are edible year-round and may be added to salads.
edibilityNote: The leaves are edible year-round and can be used in salads.

summary: A woolly flowering plant native to northern South America and introduced to the Dominican Republic. It is grown as a hothouse ornamental.

sources.title: Kohleria hirsuta (Kunth) Regel
sources.attribution: GBIF Secretariat (2023). GBIF Backbone Taxonomy. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/39omei accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-15.

summary: A low-growing flowering perennial occurring in western Europe, English stonecrop grows on dry rocks, walls, dunes and cliffs, often near the sea. Its stubby succulent leaves may turn pink in dry conditions, and its star-like flowers are white, sometimes tinged pink.

A perennial herb with no explicitly stated native origin, it grows in wet woodland or heath in northern Iberia, southwestern France and Ireland. Its rounded, heart-based leaves form a rosette at ground level, while its small white flowers are dotted yellow.
A hemiparasitic flowering plant found in western Europe and north-western Africa. It usually grows flat along the ground, with yellowish-green strap-shaped leaves and tiny yellowish flowers.

Perennial flowering plant native to Turkey and the Caucasus. It produces large, cone-shaped clusters of open, star-shaped flowers in summer, usually white or pale blue, though cultivated forms come in other colours.
Clump-forming perennial native to the Caucasus and Turkey. It has heart-shaped, toothed, gray-hairy basal leaves and white, tubular bell-shaped flowers with pointed petals.
Evergreen flowering perennial native to the Dalmatian Mountains in Croatia. It forms vigorous, low-growing mounds and produces abundant deep purple or blue flowers from mid- to late summer.

A mostly hairless perennial flowering plant predominantly native to western Europe, heath lobelia also occurs in northern Morocco and Madeira. It has shiny, toothed dark-green leaves and blue-purple flowers from May to September. It favours seasonally waterlogged, acidic ground in grassy heaths, rough pastures and open woodland.

An annual flower native to Portugal and scattered regions eastward through Europe and Asia, French speedwell has an upright, gland-covered form and small, bright blue flowers. Its broad lower leaves have weak, blunt teeth or none, becoming smaller and narrower upward, while its fruit has two deeply separated lobes.

Aquatic carnivorous perennial bladderwort of unspecified native origin, with a broad range across Europe, Asia, central and southern Africa, Australia and New Zealand. In mainland Portugal it occurs sparsely from Minho to Baixo Alentejo and was assessed as Vulnerable because of its limited occupied area, ten known locations and continuing declines.

sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

summary: A flowering herbaceous perennial native to southern Europe from Italy to western Turkey, spiny bear's-breeches has deeply cut leaves with spiny edges. In early summer it bears upright clusters of white flowers with maroon bracts.

A perennial herb occurring in western, southern and central Europe. Its roots unite into a spindle-shaped tuber, while its upright stems carry deeply divided, spiny-edged leaves and usually purple flower heads. It grows in damp meadows, marshes, banks and ditch margins.

summary: A flowering plant native to the Iberian Peninsula, reticulate thistle has received the Royal Horticultural Society’s Award of Garden Merit.

A perennial plant, viper's-grass is rare in Britain and restricted there to moist meadows in parts of England and South Wales. It has deep-yellow flower heads from May to July and exudes milky juice from its stem.

Flowering plant with two documented subspecies in Portugal: subsp. atlantica is native to mainland Portugal and Madeira but possibly introduced to the Azores, while subsp. lutescens is native to mainland Portugal.
An annual flowering plant native from Europe to western Siberia, the Himalayas and northern Africa, it grows in temperate climates.
A sunflower-family plant widespread across much of Eurasia. It is strongly aromatic, spreads mainly through creeping stems to form thick groups, and flowers very late in summer.
A perennial herb native to Europe. It has broad, divided leaves and pale-pink to purple flower rays, and grows in open forests, rocky woodland edges, scrub, meadows and fertile ground.

summary: Upright, short-lived perennial herb native to the western and eastern Cape Provinces of South Africa, within a relatively small coastal range. Its green leaves resemble holly and have irregular prickly teeth. Daisy-like heads usually carry bright-pink outer flowers, and a plant may produce several hundred heads that cover the foliage.
A flowering plant, Senecio doria includes the variety subsp. legionensis, which is native only to the Iberian Peninsula and occurs in mainland Portugal.

A perennial herb native to southeastern Europe from Greece and Italy to Ukraine and the Czech Republic, it has roundish leaves and produces its yellow flower heads one at a time. It is reportedly naturalized in Oregon.
A small perennial fern confined to western Europe and Macaronesia. It is fragile and forms large, dense colonies from creeping underground stems.
A Fuchsia species found in Brazil.
A perennial rush native to Southwestern and Central Europe, including the Alps and Pyrenees. It is grown as an ornamental grass and can escape gardens and become invasive in some climates.
A flowering plant represented in Portugal by two subspecies, both native to mainland Portugal; the nominate subspecies is introduced in the Azores. It is an annual.

A flowering plant native to South America and introduced in mainland Portugal and the Azores. Its branches and narrow, smooth-edged leaves are densely covered with close-lying hairs, while its ripe fruit is dull, dark black-purple. In Portugal it grows in shady, disturbed field margins and streamside woodland.

summary: A biennial or perennial flowering plant, it includes two subspecies in mainland Portugal that are native only to the Iberian Peninsula. Its rough, hairy foliage has strongly wavy or curled leaf edges, while its dark purple flowers turn deep blue and bloom in spring.

A small evergreen tree native to and found only in the Azores, Azores laurel is a major part of the islands’ laurel and high-elevation juniper forests. It also occurs on lava flows, in coastal and mountain scrub, and in forested peat bogs.
